_comment: Every setting a Mac has, tagged by who provides it. The window in
plugin-settings/ renders this file and nothing else, so a row can be added,
retagged or corrected without touching QML — and therefore without
`omarchy restart shell`. It is re-read every time the window opens.
tag is exactly one of:
omarchy     Omarchy already does this; the row acts or deep-links
macifier    Macifier provides it; the row acts
plugin      A published third-party plugin does it; the row offers install
planned     Nothing provides it yet; grey, inert, says which phase
notonlinux  Apple hardware or an Apple service; grey, inert, says why
RULE: a grey row (planned, notonlinux) MUST carry a note saying why, and
name the nearest Linux equivalent when one exists. A greyed row that does
not say why is just a broken one — the same rule the dock's barred tiles
follow in share/dock-placeholders.json.
action is optional and at most one of:
{"run": [...]}     argv for omarchy-macifier
{"menu": "id"}     omarchy menu summon <id>
{"plugin": "url"}  omarchy plugin add <url> --enable
Panes follow macOS System Settings' sidebar order, not Omarchy's menu
order. That is the whole point: a Mac user finds things where a Mac puts
them. Source of truth for the full inventory is docs/SETTINGS.md section 3.

rows.label: Dock
rows.omarchy: Show the dock along the bottom

rows.label: Pinned apps
rows.omarchy: Which apps keep a place in the dock

rows.label: Calendar in the Dock
rows.omarchy: Opens Chronica's agenda, when Chronica is enabled

rows.label: Indicators for open apps
rows.omarchy: A dot under every running app
rows.note: On whenever the dock is.

rows.label: Magnification
rows.note: On whenever the dock is.

rows.label: Position on screen
rows.note: Bottom only today.

rows.label: Size
rows.note: Fixed tile size today.

rows.label: Automatically hide and show
rows.note: Auto-hide is not yet a choice.

rows.label: Show recent applications
rows.note: The dock shows pinned and running apps only.

rows.label: Minimise windows using
rows.note: Hyprland has no minimise; the honest build is a scratchpad workspace. The genie effect is out of reach.

rows.label: Mission Control
rows.omarchy: Every window, spread out at once

rows.label: Stage Manager
rows.omarchy: Focused window centred, the rest set aside

rows.label: Hot Corners
rows.omarchy: Throw the pointer at a corner

rows.label: Calendar
rows.omarchy: Chronica: a synced agenda, replacing the bar clock

rows.label: Displays have separate Spaces
rows.note: Hyprland's default; nothing to switch on.

rows.label: Tiled windows
rows.note: The Mac default inverted: here windows tile unless you float them.

rows.label: Close windows when quitting an app
rows.note: Hyprland draws no line between an app and its windows, so there is no such state to keep.

rows.label: Prefer tabs when opening documents
rows.note: Decided per application, never system-wide.

rows.label: Widgets on the desktop
rows.note: No desktop layer to put them on. Closest: Omarchy's own bar widgets.

rows.label: Use F1–F12 as function keys
rows.omarchy: Brightness and volume direct, Fn for F-keys

rows.label: Keyboard brightness
rows.note: Needs Apple's backlit keyboard; confirmed on this MacBook only.

rows.label: Text Replacements
rows.note: A different model: sequences you type, not pairs you register.

rows.label: Key repeat rate and delay
rows.note: Editable in Hyprland's config today, but nothing here shows you the two numbers.

rows.label: Modifier Keys
rows.note: Remapping ⌘ ⌥ ⌃ ⇪ wholesale. Partly covered by oliverlukschander.mac-option and asaharan.omackey.

rows.label: Press 🌐 to…
rows.note: There is no Globe key outside Apple's own keyboards, so there is nothing to bind.

rows.label: Natural scrolling
rows.note: Sets it for every pointing device. Trackpad Plus sets it per trackpad, and a per-device setting wins there — so if this looks stuck, check Trackpad Plus.

rows.label: Tracking speed
rows.note: Hyprland has only a global input:sensitivity, which would drag a USB mouse along with the trackpad. Trackpad Plus sets it per device instead.

rows.label: Tap to click
rows.note: Off by default on Apple trackpads.

rows.label: Pointer acceleration
rows.note: System, Flat, Mac-inspired or a hand-drawn curve. macOS exposes none of this — it is more than the Mac gives you, not less.

rows.label: Secondary click
rows.note: Two-finger click is already the Mac behaviour. Trackpad Plus can turn it off if you would rather not have it.

rows.label: Scroll speed
rows.note: A number in Hyprland's config; Trackpad Plus puts a slider on it.

rows.label: Swipe up for Mission Control
rows.note: The gesture exists; what it opens has to be installed first.

rows.label: Turn the trackpad off
rows.note: The Mac only offers this as "ignore the built-in trackpad when a mouse is present"; here it is a plain switch.

rows.label: Force click and haptic feedback
rows.note: No force-touch driver exists for Apple Silicon trackpads. A Dell XPS haptic pad is the only one Omarchy drives.

rows.label: Bluetooth devices, pair
rows.note: AirPods need putting into pairing mode by hand the first time — lid open, hold the case button until the light blinks white. Nothing on any platform can do that part for you.

rows.label: AirPods connect when you pick them up
rows.note: Watches the unencrypted advertisement AirPods broadcast for the iPhone's pairing card, and connects when the lid opens or a bud goes in. Also tells BlueZ to identify as an Apple device, without which AirPods drop the connection after a while.

rows.label: Connect my AirPods now
rows.note: Takes them off the phone. AirPods without iCloud multipoint are a single-link headset, so whoever connects last wins.

rows.label: Release my AirPods to the iPhone
rows.note: Disconnects and stops trusting them for a few minutes, which is what makes it stick — a plain disconnect is undone within seconds by the buds asking to come back. Also in the Macifier bar widget, since that is the thing you reach for on the way out.

rows.label: AirPods battery, ANC, ear detection
rows.note: Per-pod and case battery plus the listening controls macOS keeps in its Sound menu. Builds the LibrePods daemon, which is the part Macifier deliberately does not reimplement.

rows.label: Hearing aid and Conversation Boost
rows.note: LibrePods implements these over Apple's accessory protocol; upstream notes the hearing-aid path is the least finished part on Linux.

rows.label: Announce notifications on AirPods
rows.note: Would need a text-to-speech hook on the notification daemon. Nothing reads notifications aloud on Omarchy today; the nearest piece is piper.

rows.label: Find My AirPods
rows.note: The Find My network is an Apple service keyed to an iCloud account. Closest: the last-seen signal strength in the omarchy-pods panel, which tells you warmer or colder and nothing more.

rows.label: Audio Sharing with a second pair
rows.note: Apple splits one stream across two pairs inside its own silicon. BlueZ can connect two sinks but cannot keep them in sync; LE Audio broadcast is the eventual answer and no shipping AirPods speak it.

rows.label: Spatial Audio and head tracking
rows.note: The head-tracking gyroscope data is readable, but the renderer that turns it into positional audio is Apple's. No open implementation exists.
